tools.name: qae_chat
tools.description: Talk to the QAEverest QA copilot — the same assistant as the QAEverest panel in VS Code, Cursor and JetBrains, with the same project context, conversation history and tools. Use this for anything expressed as a request: generating functional/API/UI/mobile test cases, building an automation suite, running one, or asking about a previous run. It decides which QA operation is needed and asks for anything mandatory that is missing. May return `needs_input` (ask the user, then call again with `answers`) or `awaiting_approval` (ask the user, then call `qae_approve`). Billed operations only run after an approval.

message.description: What to ask, in plain English — exactly what you'd type in the panel.

files.description: Paths to attach as context (relative to the project root or absolute). Stories, specs, OpenAPI/Postman files; PDF, DOCX and XLSX are read as text.

answers.description: Replies to a previous `needs_input` result, as an object keyed by each request's `key` (e.g. {"prompt.search_the_codebase": "how does login work"}). Omit on a first call.

tools.name: qae_approve
tools.description: Settle an approval that `qae_chat` returned as `awaiting_approval`. ONLY call this after the user has actually said yes or no — the approval exists so a human authorises spending credits or starting a real run, and answering it yourself defeats it. Returns the rest of the turn that was waiting.

id.description: The approval id from the `awaiting_approval` reply (e.g. `cf1`).

tools.name: qae_new_chat
tools.description: Start a fresh QAEverest conversation. Use when switching to an unrelated feature — the copilot replays the transcript as context, so a stale one steers it wrong. History is kept in `.qaeverest/chats/`.

tools.name: qae_history
tools.description: List this project's QAEverest conversations, newest first, with the id `qae_open_chat` takes.

tools.name: qae_open_chat
tools.description: Make an earlier conversation active again, so the copilot picks up its context.

tools.name: qae_generate_testcases
tools.description: Generate QA test cases from a user story or feature description in one call. Returns structured scenarios covering positive, negative and edge cases. Use this when the request is already clear; use `qae_chat` when it needs the copilot to work out what to do. Consumes credits. Takes 1-3 minutes.

story.description: The user story, requirement, or feature description. More detail produces better coverage (acceptance criteria, validation rules, edge conditions).

test_type.description: The kind of testing to generate for. Integration is system integration testing (SIT): how services, APIs, message queues and third-party systems work together. Database tests the database itself (schema and constraints, CRUD and referential integrity, transactions, migrations, data quality); a story that only stores data is not Database. Database cases are written from the story alone, as no database connection is passed here: name the tables and columns in `story`.

tc_type.description: Whether the cases are written for manual execution or as automation-ready scenarios.

additional.description: Extra instructions for the AI: focus areas, constraints, known edge cases.

tools.name: qae_generate_api_tests
tools.description: Generate API test cases from a plain description of the API, OR an OpenAPI/Swagger spec or Postman collection pasted as text. Returns automation-ready scenarios (positive, negative, boundary, auth). Consumes credits. Takes 1-3 minutes.

spec.description: A description of the API/endpoint to test, OR an OpenAPI/Swagger spec or Postman collection as text.

additional.description: Extra instructions for the AI: focus areas, constraints, known edge cases.

tools.name: qae_generate_ui_tests
tools.description: Generate end-to-end UI automation test cases (navigate / click / type / assert steps) from a scenario or user story. This GENERATES the cases — it does not drive a live browser. Runs as a background job and may take a few minutes. Consumes credits.

story.description: The UI scenario or user story to generate end-to-end test cases for.

additional.description: Extra instructions for the AI: focus areas, constraints, known edge cases.

tools.name: qae_generate_mobile_tests
tools.description: Generate mobile UI automation test cases (gestures, device states, platform-specific behaviour) from a scenario or user story. This GENERATES the cases — it does not drive a live device. Runs as a background job and may take a few minutes. Consumes credits.

story.description: The mobile scenario or user story to generate test cases for.

additional.description: Extra instructions for the AI: focus areas, constraints, known edge cases.

tools.name: qae_scan_project
tools.description: Build a Repo Map of this project — languages, frameworks, entry points and the files worth testing. Purely local: no network, no credits. Run this first when you want QAEverest's other tools grounded in the actual codebase rather than a description of it.

tools.name: qae_index_project
tools.description: Index the project into QAEverest's retrieval layer so generation can cite real code. Incremental by default — only changed files are sent. Requires a connected account and a reachable backend.

full.description: Re-send every file instead of only what changed. Use when the store was reset or looks stale.

tools.name: qae_search_project
tools.description: Semantic search over the indexed codebase — ask in plain English ("how does login work") and get the files and line ranges that answer it. Run `qae_index_project` first; without an index this returns nothing.

query.description: What to look for, in plain English.

answers.description: Replies to a previous `needs_input` result, as an object keyed by each request's `key` (e.g. {"prompt.search_the_codebase": "how does login work"}). Omit on a first call.

tools.name: qae_build_inventory
tools.description: Analyze the project module by module and produce a ranked inventory of testable features, each with the source files it was derived from. Takes a few minutes on a large repo. Feed the ids it returns to `qae_generate_from_features`.

tools.name: qae_select_features
tools.description: Re-display the feature inventory built earlier, with the ids needed to generate from it. Shows a sample inventory if none has been built yet. Local only.

tools.name: qae_generate_from_features
tools.description: Generate test cases for specific features from the inventory. Each feature's cited source files are read and sent as grounding, so the cases describe what the code actually does. Consumes credits. Requires `qae_build_inventory` or `qae_select_features` to have run in this session — the ids come from there.

feature_ids.description: Ids from the inventory listing, e.g. [0, 3, 7].

tools.name: qae_list_suites
tools.description: List the automation suites on this QAEverest account, with the ids `qae_run_suite` needs.

tools.name: qae_run_suite
tools.description: Execute an automation suite. This starts a REAL run against a real environment and consumes credits, so only call it when the user has explicitly asked to run something and has named the target. Mobile suites go through the device/app gate and may come back asking for setup. Only run against hosts you are authorized to test.

suite_title.description: Suite title, for the run's label and report.

base_url.description: The environment to run against. Required for web/API suites; ignored for mobile.

suite_type.description: e.g. ApiAutomation, UiAutomation, MobileAutomation — decides which engine runs it.

answers.description: Replies to a previous `needs_input` result, as an object keyed by each request's `key` (e.g. {"prompt.search_the_codebase": "how does login work"}). Omit on a first call.

tools.name: qae_save_report
tools.description: Write the HTML execution report for the last finished run into `qaeverest-reports/` in the project, with per-test steps, durations and trend. Needs a run to have finished in this session.

tools.name: qae_open_report
tools.description: Report the path of the most recently saved HTML execution report so it can be opened or read.

tools.name: qae_agent_suites
tools.description: List the saved AI Agent Testing suites on this account — the agent each one tests and whether a drift baseline is pinned — with the ids `qae_agent_run` needs. Needs a personal API key. Costs nothing.

tools.name: qae_agent_run
tools.description: Run a saved AI agent suite against the agent (or another endpoint, e.g. staging). This sends REAL conversations to that agent and consumes credits, so only call it when the user has explicitly asked to run the suite, and only against an agent they are authorized to test. Returns at once with a run id; the run takes minutes — follow it with `qae_agent_run_status`.

endpoint.description: Run against this endpoint instead of the suite's saved agent; the saved request format is reused.

agent_api_key.description: The agent's own API key, if it needs one. Used for this run only, never stored.

tools.name: qae_agent_run_status
tools.description: Progress of an AI agent run, then its trust score, release gate and verdict (pending | pass | fail | error) with the reasons. The optional thresholds tighten the verdict like the CI gate's. Costs nothing.

max_breaches.description: Fail with more guardrail breaches than this.

fail_on_no_baseline.description: Fail when there's no comparable pinned baseline, instead of warning.

tools.name: qae_security_scan
tools.description: Run a QAEverest security scan against a live URL — security headers, SSL/TLS, and common vulnerability checks — and return risk-rated findings. Consumes credits. ONLY scan hosts the user is authorized to test; if there is any doubt whose host it is, ask before calling.

url.description: The target, including http:// or https://.

scan_type.description: Which checks to run. `full` runs all of them.

headers.description: Extra request headers, e.g. an Authorization header for an authenticated endpoint.

tools.name: qae_performance_test
tools.description: Run a load, stress, spike or soak test against a live URL and report latency percentiles, throughput and error rate. Pass the user's wording in `message` and the settings are read out of it, or set them explicitly — an explicit field wins. Server caps keep a single call bounded (about a minute). Consumes credits and generates REAL traffic against the target, so only run it against hosts the user is authorized to load-test.

url.description: The target, including http:// or https://.

message.description: The user's request in their own words; mode, virtual users and duration are read out of it.

method.description: HTTP method for each request. Default GET.

virtual_users.description: Concurrent virtual users (load/soak). Server caps apply.

duration.description: Duration in seconds. Server caps apply (load ≤ 60s, soak ≤ 90s).

headers.description: Request headers as a key/value object.

tools.name: qae_mobile_setup
tools.description: Configure mobile automation — device farm credentials, the app binary, and which handset to run on. The setup form is an interactive page, which a tool call has no surface for, so this returns the link to it in the QAEverest web app along with the profiles already configured.

tools.name: qae_status
tools.description: Show whether QAEverest is connected, which backend and project it uses, the key type, credits used and remaining, requests this month, which services are enabled for the key, and any settings that would make this machine behave differently from another. Also collects output from a long operation that was still running when a previous tool call returned. Costs nothing.

tools.name: qae_connect
tools.description: Store a QAEverest API key for this machine, or start browser sign-in. With `api_key`, the key is validated and saved to ~/.qaeverest/credentials.json (mode 0600). Without one, a device-flow sign-in starts and this returns a URL and a code for the USER to approve in their browser — call it again with no arguments afterwards to finish. Never invent or guess a key.

api_key.description: A `qae_...` key the user supplied. Omit to use browser sign-in instead.

tools.name: qae_disconnect
tools.description: Forget the stored QAEverest API key on this machine. Does not touch the account itself.
